heading: One structure check before the build
body:
Before Tachyon writes any output or starts a compiler such as `dart`, `cargo`, `go` or `dotnet`, it checks the structure of the whole project. It reads every file in every role folder of both realms, at any depth, and it reports the problems of all files in one run. Each message names the file, points at the class or the import, and gives the fix in the spelling of your language.

| The check | Code | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A class in a role folder has the marker of that folder. | `TY1363` | Add the marker, such as `@Service`, `#[Service]`, `[<Service>]`, `-- @Service` or `// @yon::Service`, or move a plain class to `models` or a utility folder. |
| A marked class ends with its role name and sits in its role folder: `Service`, `Store`, `Client`, `Helper`, `Converter`, `Setup`, `Entity` or `Controller`. | `TY1310` | Rename the class `Mail` to `MailService` and the file to `MailService.rb` in a `services` folder. |
| The file has the name of its class, in the file name style of its language. | `TY1318` | Rename `Order.ts` that declares `Invoice`; Rust may write `mail_service.rs`. |
| A role file holds one class: in Go a struct with its methods, in Lua a class table, in F# a type, in Rust a type with its `impl` blocks. | `TY1310` | Move the second class to its own file. |
| Dependencies point down, nothing needs a controller, and a utility class names no role class. | `TY1327` | Give the utility the value it needs as a parameter, or move the code into a service. |
| A file never imports a file of the other realm. | `TY1369` | Call the server through an HTTPClient in `client/remotes`, and give each realm its own model, utility or service. |

Some files keep their own rules, so they need no role marker: models, which only hold data; utility classes in `client/shared/utils` and `server/utils`; test units and test setups; generated files; the native Go module in `server/packages`; and the data, styles, scripts and assets in `client/shared`. A folder that is not a role folder, such as `server/commands`, never needs a marker.

`ty migrate check` lists missing markers, imports of the other realm and dependency problems, and `ty migrate fix --write` renames a file whose class has another name.
